item.problem_title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
item.problem_statement: Electronic health records arise from encounters, billing and documentation rather than from scheduled research assessments, so eligibility and follow-up in an emulation partly reflect care-seeking and access rather than the biology the protocol intends. Whether a given database can support a given target trial is a question about the data source and the protocol jointly, and quantitative assessments of that pair now exist. What does not exist is a prespecified stop rule: a threshold agreed before the analysis, on observability, temporal precision, capture continuity, comparator support, outcome validity and linkage completeness, that would halt a study when an essential component fails. item.paper: Invited Commentary: Influenza, Influenza Immunization, and Pregnancy-It's About Time.
item.evidence: This is a data-fitness criterion of the kind usually missing: it names two specific variables, the calendar time of viral circulation and the gestational age at vaccination, and states that without them the study should not be undertaken. It is stated for one exposure and one outcome family and derived from the biology rather than from a general procedure, so it does not generalize on its own.
item.quote:
We present a framework to avoid time-related biases in the study
of influenza illness and immunization in pregnancy and advise that investigations of fetal benefit from maternal influenza immunization should only be undertaken when information is available on the calendar time of influenza virus
circulation and the gestational age at which maternal influenza immunization occurred.

verdicts.reason: The quotation establishes alignment of eligibility, assignment, and follow-up at time zero. It supplies no outcome-blind rule for selecting interval width or grace-period duration, which are the unresolved quantities in this problem.

item.problem_title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
item.problem_statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act, when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins, and it has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as scheduled visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation handle the misalignment; neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. Selection tools exist and use outcome information: cross-validated variance has been evaluated as a measure of data support for choosing a discretization. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation proc
item.paper: Specifying a target trial prevents immortal time bias and other self-inflicted injuries in observational analyses.
item.evidence: The alignment principle removes immortal time by construction and is the foundation the rest of the field builds on. What it does not supply is any rule for the grid on which time zero and subsequent decisions are placed, or for how long a grace period may run before the data stop being consistent with a strategy; the paper takes the strategies and their timing as given.

verdicts.reason: Comparing multiple estimators through simulation partially informs estimator choice under the simulated favorable setting. It neither establishes a general default nor requires analysts to demonstrate how their substantive estimate depends on estimator choice.

item.problem_title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
item.problem_statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: n

item.problem_title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
item.problem_statement: The canonical protocol has seven linked components: eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan. Conceptual specification and operational realization are distinct, and when a component cannot be observed the analyst substitutes a proxy. If no valid measurement, missing-data or validation model recovers the intended variable, the resulting observed-data functional generally does not identify the intended causal effect, and it does not automatically identify some other one either: naming it a different estimand requires a corresponding intervention and an identification argument. A criterion that cannot be verified is dropped and the population changes; a strategy that cannot be distinguished from its neighbor is merged and the contrast changes; an outcome that is only partly captured redefines the endpoint. verdicts.reason: Declaring some whole drug-comparator comparisons unevaluable for inadequate balance is not a history-specific positivity diagnostic. The quotation does not support the asserted prespecified criteria, localization by time and history, or a surviving restricted-population estimand.

item.problem_title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
item.problem_statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software
item.paper: Critical evaluation of real-world evidence of repurposable medicines in the Alzheimer's disease drug development pipeline using a target trial emulation.
item.evidence: Three positivity and balance criteria were fixed in advance and enforced, and the enforcement had teeth: some drug and comparator pairs were declared not evaluable rather than reported with unstable weights, semaglutide among them. What the diagnostics do not do is identify which patient histories lack support, so a failure removes a whole comparison rather than naming the region.
item.quote: Moreover, some drugs were not evaluable across both cohorts or specific comparator groups due to inadequate covariate balance.

verdicts.reason: A validated generic quality checklist is a real partial precursor to decision criteria for observational evidence. It does not provide prespecified, decision-specific regulatory acceptance criteria for protocol fidelity, residual confounding, or robustness.

item.problem_title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
item.problem_statement: FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. None supplies an acceptance criterion, and a universal numerical cutoff for emulation adequacy, residual confounding or sensitivity-analysis sufficiency would not be technically defensible if one were offered. What is missing is the defensible version: prespecified, decision-specific criteria covering protocol fidelity, identification plausibility, data fitness, diagnostics, quantitative bias analysis and robustness of the decision itself, agreed before the submission rather than argued after it. item.paper: The GRACE Checklist: A Validated Assessment Tool for High Quality Observational Studies of Comparative Effectiveness.
item.evidence: This is the closest thing the field has to a threshold: a screening instrument with measured sensitivity and specificity against external criteria, distinguished from the surrounding guidance documents by having been validated at all. The comparison table lists eight guidance documents developed by consensus alone. What the instrument screens for is publication-level quality, not whether an estimate is adequate for a specific regulatory decision, which the paper states it cannot assess.
item.quote:
Although many guidance documents have been developed for
the evaluation of observational study quality, only the GRACE
Checklist has been validated against external measures of quality.

verdicts.reason: The checklist's consistent emphasis on sensitivity analyses partially standardizes reporting of dependence on assumptions. It does not distinguish diagnosable from undiagnosable assumptions or provide the structured, design-specific diagnostic panel the problem requires.

item.problem_title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
item.problem_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.
item.paper: The GRACE Checklist: A Validated Assessment Tool for High Quality Observational Studies of Comparative Effectiveness.
item.evidence: The checklist item that predicted quality in all four trees is whether the study reported sensitivity analyses showing how much the estimate depended on its assumptions, which is a partial assumption dashboard: it records that dependence was examined without distinguishing assumptions that can be diagnosed from those that cannot.
item.quote: Only sensitivity analyses appeared consistently as a predictor of quality in all 4 trees.

item.paper: Statins and Risk of Lower Limb Revision Surgery: The Influence of Differences in Study Design Using Electronic Health Records From the United Kingdom and Denmark.
item.evidence: Running the same protocol on two national databases with different structures is a data-fitness check performed rather than described, and it returned a negative result: rate ratios agreed although absolute revision rates did not, which the paper attributes to underrecording in general practice records. The check is post hoc and would not have stopped the study.
item.quote: The use of different data sources was not a discriminating factor in this example of statins and implant revision.
